# Gezel Help

> Gezel is a free, open-source app and platform for running a crew of AI agents on your own computer, with local models or a cloud plan you already have. Every article below is plain markdown.

To build a Gezel app, read [Build a Gezel app: the complete guide](https://gezel.com/docs/build-a-gezel-app.md) first. It holds the working loop, the rules, and the four app-building guides in full.

## Concepts

- [What is gezel?](https://gezel.com/docs/welcome.md): AI help with a name, a face, and a role, working for you from your own computer.
- [Your crew: the Meester, who runs each project, and everyone else](https://gezel.com/docs/the-crew.md): Who's who on your crew, and how the roles fit together.
- [Social mode: character, growth, and what's waiting](https://gezel.com/docs/character-and-growth.md): How each crew member's character shapes their chat, how they grow with you, and the one switch that turns it all on or off.
- [Projects, threads, and where work lives](https://gezel.com/docs/projects-and-threads.md): How gezel organizes work, and where the results end up.
- [Memory, documents, and the shared library](https://gezel.com/docs/memory-and-documents.md): What Gezel remembers, and where shared knowledge lives.
- [Documents: make and convert Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files](https://gezel.com/docs/making-documents.md): Ask Gezel to make a Word, PowerPoint, Excel, or PDF file, or to convert files you already have into DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and more.
- [Plans: procedures Gezel can follow](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbooks-overview.md): Repeatable, checkable, multi-step work — written down like a recipe.
- [Models, tiers, and what runs on this device](https://gezel.com/docs/local-models-and-tiers.md): Cloud or local, big or small — how gezel matches models to work.
- [Tasks, scheduled work, and supervision](https://gezel.com/docs/tasks-and-supervision.md): Work that runs without you watching — and the guardrails around it.
- [Adding folders: give Gezel something to look after](https://gezel.com/docs/adding-folders.md): Hand Gezel a folder; it reads the files, works on them overnight, and never changes one.
- [Views: see what's in a folder](https://gezel.com/docs/project-views.md): The Views tab shows a project's files as a village, a diagram, shelves, a timeline, or the reports written about them.
- [The Night Shift: work Gezel does while you sleep](https://gezel.com/docs/night-shift.md): A nightly window for quiet background work — and the roles that bring their own.
- [Notifications: only when something happened](https://gezel.com/docs/notifications.md): What gezel notifies you about, how often, and how to turn it down or off.
- [Cameras and lookouts: keep an eye on a room](https://gezel.com/docs/cameras-and-lookouts.md): Connect a webcam to a project, let gezel notice what happens in view, and tell it what to do when it sees something.
- [Local-first: your data stays on your disk](https://gezel.com/docs/privacy-local-first.md): No gezel cloud, no hidden database — files you can open and back up.
- [Integrations: let other tools use Gezel](https://gezel.com/docs/connected-apps.md): Editors and other programs can talk to Gezel through standard AI endpoints — with your approval, on your terms.
- [Generalist mode](https://gezel.com/docs/generalist-mode.md): One pair of hands carries a task from first step to last in a single conversation.

## Crew roles

- [Roles at a glance](https://gezel.com/docs/roles-index.md): Every built-in role, what it does, and what it needs.
- [The Meester](https://gezel.com/docs/role/meester.md): The guildmaster — your front door to the whole crew.
- [Every role template](https://gezel.com/docs/role-catalog.md): Ready-made characters you can add to your crew, from researcher to meal planner.
- [The Crew Lead](https://gezel.com/docs/role/voorman.md): Runs one project's crew so you don't have to.
- [The Reviewer](https://gezel.com/docs/role/reviewer.md): The quality gate — verifies claims before anything ships.
- [The Researcher](https://gezel.com/docs/role/researcher.md): Digs into questions and comes back with sourced answers.
- [The Copywriter](https://gezel.com/docs/role/copywriter.md): Drafts and reworks words — on brief, on tone, on length.
- [The Designer](https://gezel.com/docs/role/designer.md): Shapes visual deliverables and places imagery where it belongs.
- [The Image Generator](https://gezel.com/docs/role/image-generator.md): A fixed-function specialist — prompts in, pictures out.
- [The Video Generator](https://gezel.com/docs/role/video-generator.md): Short clips from prompts — the moving-picture sibling.
- [The Developer](https://gezel.com/docs/role/developer.md): Builds and fixes code, held to build-and-test gates.
- [The Web Developer](https://gezel.com/docs/role/web-developer.md): Frontend and full-stack work with a live browser in the loop.
- [The Planner](https://gezel.com/docs/role/planner.md): Turns a fuzzy brief into a structured, checkable plan.
- [The Generalist](https://gezel.com/docs/role/generalist.md): Carries a whole task from first step to last in one conversation.
- [The Conversationalist](https://gezel.com/docs/role/conversationalist.md): Talks things through with you, looking things up when it helps.
- [The Curator](https://gezel.com/docs/role/curator.md): Looks after your photos and proposes albums, without moving a file.

## Plans

- [Every plan](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbooks-index.md): All the step-by-step procedures Gezel can follow.
- [A/B Ad Copy Variations](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/ad-variations.md): Generate a set of distinct, testable ad-copy variations for one offer across the angles worth A/B testing: it first locks the platform and its constraints (headline/description character limits), the offer, audience, and the distinct messaging angles to test (benefit, pain, social proof, urgency, curiosity), then drafts multiple complete variants per angle so each is a genuine test of a hypothesis rather than a trivial reword.
- [A/B Test Readout](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/ab-test-readout.md): Analyze a controlled experiment and produce a decision-ready readout: does the variant beat control, by how much, and is it real? States the hypothesis, the primary metric, and the decision rule FIRST (to avoid p-hacking and metric-shopping), then computes lift, statistical significance, and confidence intervals as a data-analyst, then writes a plain-language ship/no-ship recommendation.
- [Accessibility Audit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/a11y-audit.md): Audit a web page or UI for accessibility against WCAG 2.1 AA and produce a prioritized remediation report.
- [Accessibility Retrofit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/accessibility-retrofit.md): Audit real pages for concrete accessibility violations — alt text, labels, heading order, keyboard and focus, landmarks, contrast — then fix each one at its real site in the markup and verify it, with an enforced independent review that rejects accessibility theater.
- [Animated Content Slideshow](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/narrated-slideshow.md): Turn written content into a real MP4 video and animated GIF with DocBlocks.
- [Animated SVG / CSS Hero](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/svg-animation.md): Build a single-file animated SVG or CSS hero section — a looping illustrated scene, an animated logo, or a motion banner driven by CSS keyframes or SMIL with no JavaScript animation library.
- [Anniversary Cut](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/anniversary-cut.md): Build the highlight reel for the occasion: the archive queried for the person and the years that matter, clips chosen with stated reasons, assembled through the project's media pipeline with a run log, and delivered with a chapter list and a dedication — the reel that makes the birthday.
- [Annotated Bibliography](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/annotated-bibliography.md): Build a formal annotated bibliography for a research topic: a planner locks the scope, the citation style, and the annotation rubric (summary + evaluation + relevance), then a researcher locates each source and writes a consistent, properly-formatted annotation that summarizes, critically evaluates, and situates it for the research question.
- [Annual Document Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/annual-document-review.md): Walk a life binder's document roster once a year: inventory what is present and missing, confirm each present document is still current (right beneficiaries, right address, not expired), record the review so staleness tracking resets, and produce a prioritized to-do for the gaps.
- [Anomaly / Outlier Scan](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/anomaly-scan.md): Scan a dataset for anomalies and outliers and report what is genuinely unusual versus expected noise.
- [Answer a Question with SQL](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/sql-analysis.md): Answer a specific business question against a database or table set with a correct, readable SQL query and a short written answer.
- [API Contract Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/api-contract-review.md): Review an API contract or specification (OpenAPI/REST/GraphQL) for correctness, consistency, and developer ergonomics, then produce a findings report.
- [Apply Review Findings](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/apply-review-findings.md): Take an existing review's findings and close them for real: triage each one against the current code, fix the real ones at their actual sites with the smallest correct change, verify per finding, and account for every finding end to end under an enforced review.
- [Artifact Integrity & Ship Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/artifact-integrity-review.md): Perform an isolated ship-readiness review of the actual built artifacts of a project—sites, npm packages, archives, CLIs, binaries, installers, checksums, signatures, and release bundles—rather than trusting source or CI status.
- [Audio Ad Spot](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/audio-ad-spot.md): Produce a short broadcast/podcast audio ad spot (15s/30s/60s) — a tightly-timed script with a hook, value, and a single call-to-action, synthesized into a finished, runtime-accurate voiced spot with optional music bed cue.
- [Audio Highlight Reel](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/audio-highlight-reel.md): Cut a long recording (podcast, interview, talk, stream) down to a short highlight reel of its best moments, delivered as a single stitched audio clip plus a cue sheet of the segments used.
- [Audit Evidence Pack](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/audit-evidence-pack.md): Assemble an audit-ready evidence pack from a compliance register: every obligation in scope with its owner, due date, status and the proof on file, the gaps ranked by how soon they bite, and the next step for each.
- [Audit Recurring Subscriptions](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/subscription-audit.md): Audit a set of transactions or a vendor list to find every recurring subscription, normalize each to a monthly cost, surface duplicates, price hikes, and zombie/unused services, and produce a prioritized cancel/keep recommendation report.
- [Auth / Session Implementation](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/auth-flow.md): Implement an authentication and session flow — login, session/token issuance, verification, and logout — with the security fundamentals baked in.
- [Automate a Booking or Checkout Flow](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/booking-automation.md): Automate a multi-step booking, reservation, or checkout flow end-to-end — select, fill details, choose options, confirm — with a hard dry-run/confirmation guard so it never accidentally commits a real transaction during development.
- [Batch Image Transform](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/image-batch-edit.md): Apply a consistent transform across a whole folder of images — resize, crop to a ratio, convert format, compress, watermark, or recolor — and verify every file came out correct.
- [Batch-Fill Forms from a Dataset](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/form-fill-batch.md): Automate filling a web or PDF form once per row of an input dataset — registrations, applications, data-entry portals, mail-merge into a form.
- [Behavior-Preserving Refactor](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/refactor-module.md): Restructure code without changing what it does, with proof at every stage: a green suite recorded before anything moves (characterization tests pinned first when coverage is thin), small reversible stages that keep the tests green, a re-measured structure target, and an enforced independent review.
- [Board Meeting Deck](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/board-deck.md): Build a board-meeting deck that briefs directors efficiently — an executive summary up top, KPI dashboard, financials, progress against goals, key risks/asks, and an appendix — structured so a director gets the state of the business in minutes.
- [Brand Tone Rewrite](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/tone-rewrite.md): Re-voice existing content to a specific brand tone while preserving every fact and the original structure: it first codifies the target voice into a concrete style guide — adjectives, do's and don'ts, banned and preferred words, sentence-length feel, point of view — then rewrites the content line by line to that voice without changing what it says.
- [Branding Website](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/branding-website.md): Build a small brand/marketing website where the visual identity leads.
- [Browser Extension](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/chrome-extension.md): Build a Manifest V3 browser extension scaffold — a popup, a content script, and the manifest — that does one concrete thing on the current page (highlight, count, extract, or toggle).
- [Browser QA Audit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/browser-qa-audit.md): Exercise a running app in a real browser, triage what breaks, and produce a report-only QA findings list with a health score — no code changes.
- [Build + Test a Tricky Regex](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/regex-builder.md): Build a regular expression that matches exactly the right strings and rejects the wrong ones — specified with concrete should-match and should-NOT-match cases before a single character is written.
- [Build Loop](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/build-loop.md): Generic make-something procedure: scope the work and lock concrete acceptance criteria, build it, evaluate the result against those criteria, and loop back to building until every criterion is met — then finish.
- [Bulk CRM Update from Notes](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/crm-update-batch.md): Turn unstructured notes (call logs, meeting recaps, email threads) into a batch of structured CRM updates: per-contact field changes, activity logs, and next-step tasks as a validated import file.
- [Bulk Product Descriptions](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/product-descriptions.md): Generate consistent, on-brand product descriptions in bulk from a list of products and their attributes: it first locks the brand voice, the field schema (title, short blurb, long description, bullet features, SEO meta), and a worked exemplar, then drafts every product to that exact template so the whole catalog reads as one voice.
- [Canvas Generative Art](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/canvas-generative-art.md): Build a single-file generative art piece on canvas — flow fields, particle systems, recursive trees, Voronoi, noise terrain, or geometric tilings — that produces a fresh composition each run from a seed, with parameters the viewer can tweak.
- [Capture a Recipe Card](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/recipe-capture.md): Rescue a handwritten recipe card without sanding off its soul: transcribe the original faithfully — spelling quirks, margin notes, and all — standardize quantities in a separate block alongside (never instead of) the original wording, and pin the provenance note: whose card, whose kitchen, what they always changed.
- [Care Visit Prep](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/visit-prep.md): Prepare a one-page brief for a medical or care appointment from the project's care record: compile everything logged since the last visit, the current medication list with doses, the changes and symptoms worth raising, and a prioritized question list — so the ten minutes in the room get spent on what matters.
- [Careful Mode](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/careful-mode.md): Safety guardrails for destructive commands.
- [Catalog an Item](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/item-intake.md): Take new arrivals from shoebox to catalog: identify each item from its photo notes, record it with condition and an honest value basis, and flag what needs a better photo or an expert eye — uncertain identification stays uncertain in the record instead of becoming confident fiction.
- [Categorize Transactions](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/expense-categorize.md): Classify a list of bank/card transactions into a fixed chart-of-accounts category set, with confidence and a review queue for the uncertain ones, producing a clean categorized ledger ready for bookkeeping or tax.
- [Character Sheet](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/character-sheet.md): Lock a character before the pages need them: reference images across the poses and expressions the story calls for, the palette and silhouette written down, and every seed and prompt persisted in a manifest — so page twelve's hero is page one's hero.
- [Character Turnaround](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/character-turnaround.md): Give one character the full turnaround treatment: front, side, back, and three-quarter views generated against the same style anchor, every view manifest-recorded with the seed and prompt that made it — the reference every future sprite leans on.
- [Chart Pack from Data](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/chart-pack.md): Build a single interactive HTML page of charts that answers a defined set of questions about a dataset.
- [CI Pipeline from Scratch](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/ci-pipeline.md): Author a CI pipeline grounded in what the repo actually has: inventory the real package scripts, write the workflow at the conventional location with caching and merge-gating on green, and verify every command it invokes against the manifests — honest that CI itself cannot run locally.
- [Citation Audit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/citation-audit.md): Audit an existing document's claims against its citations and report every mismatch: a reviewer pairs each cited claim with the citation it depends on and locks the audit rubric, a researcher opens each cited source and verifies the claim is actually supported, and a reviewer compiles a per-citation audit report with verdicts and fixes.
- [Cited Research Report](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/research-report.md): Produce a rigorously cited research report that answers a specific question end to end: a planner first decomposes the question into sub-questions and locks the scope, then a researcher gathers and logs primary and secondary sources with inline citations, then a copywriter writes a structured markdown report (executive summary, findings, evidence, limitations, references).
- [Classify and Route Incoming Documents](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/doc-intake-pipeline.md): Build a document-intake pipeline that classifies each incoming file (invoice, contract, resume, receipt, ID, support ticket, other) into a fixed type set, extracts a few key fields per type, and routes it to the right destination folder with a normalized filename.
- [Clean a Dataset](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/dataset-clean.md): Profile, clean, and validate a messy CSV/TSV/JSON dataset into an analysis-ready table.
- [Close the Month](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/month-close.md): Close out a month of household spending against the project's ledger: sweep the month's entries for category strays and surprises, compute the in/out/net totals and category breakdown, compare against the prior month, and write a short honest month summary with one concrete action for next month.
- [Code Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/code-review.md): Snapshot-driven code review.
- [Codebase Refactoring Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/codebase-refactoring-review.md): Review an entire codebase for the least cogent, highest-leverage refactoring opportunities without changing source.
- [Codebase UX Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/codebase-ux-review.md): Review the user experience implemented across a codebase and, when runnable, exercise the key flows in a real browser.
- [Codemod Sweep](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/codemod-sweep.md): Make a mechanical change everywhere it applies - a rename, an API-call migration, dead-code removal: enumerate every site first, apply the change under stated invariants, then re-scan to prove zero un-excluded sites remain, with counts that reconcile exactly and a green suite as receipts.
- [Coherent Icon Pack](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/icon-pack.md): Produce a coherent set of UI icons that look like they belong to one family — consistent grid, stroke weight, corner radius, optical sizing, and metaphor language — from a named list of concepts.
- [Cohort / Retention Analysis](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/cohort-analysis.md): Analyze retention or behavior by cohort to reveal whether the product is getting stickier over time.
- [Command-Line Tool](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/cli-tool.md): Build a command-line tool with subcommands, flags, arguments, help text, and proper exit codes.
- [Company Research Brief](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/company-research-brief.md): A sharp, dated, sourced brief on a company before an interview or application — what they do and how they make money, recent signals, team and role context, culture as evidenced, likely interview themes, and five specific questions to ask THEM.
- [Compatibility Check](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/compat-check.md): Answer 'does it still work on the new version?' with a matrix, not a shrug: the datapack's files checked against each target version's format rules, every break named with the exact file and the exact fix, and the upgrade path written down in order.
- [Competitive Analysis](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/competitive-analysis.md): Compare a set of competitors across consistent dimensions and turn the comparison into an actionable analysis: a planner locks the competitor set and the evaluation dimensions, a researcher fills a feature/positioning matrix with evidence-backed cells, and a copywriter writes the analysis with a clear recommendation and competitive gaps.
- [Comprehensive Codebase Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/comprehensive-codebase-review.md): The definitive deep, consultant-level review of an entire codebase and its architecture.
- [Containerize a Service](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/dockerize-app.md): Containerize an application with a production-grade Dockerfile — small, secure, reproducible, and buildable — plus the supporting files to run it.
- [Content Accuracy Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/content-accuracy-review.md): Fact-check a piece of content for accuracy and produce a claim-by-claim verification report.
- [Contract Template (Non-Legal-Advice)](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/contract-template.md): Draft a reusable, plain-language agreement template — service agreement, NDA, freelance contract, or terms — with clearly marked fill-in fields, structured numbered clauses, and a prominent non-legal-advice disclaimer.
- [Corpus Synthesis](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/corpus-synthesis.md): Read a provided corpus of documents and synthesize it into a single coherent overview: a planner sets the synthesis question and the extraction schema, a researcher reads every document and extracts structured notes keyed back to each source, and a copywriter synthesizes the extracts into a unified narrative organized by idea rather than by document.
- [CRUD Web App](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/web-app-crud.md): Build a small single-file CRUD web app — a todo list, notes, contacts, or inventory manager — with create, read, update, and delete plus localStorage persistence so data survives a reload.
- [CSV / Tabular Transformer](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/csv-transformer.md): Reshape and convert tabular data from one schema to another: rename and reorder columns, split or merge fields, derive new columns, pivot/unpivot, change format (CSV<->JSON<->TSV), and filter rows.
- [Curate an Album](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/album-curate.md): Turn a thousand camera-roll photos into the forty that tell the story: cull the near-duplicates, keep the keepers for honest reasons, caption what matters, and leave an album manifest the family will actually revisit.
- [Curated Annotated Reading List](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/reading-list.md): Curate an annotated reading list on a topic for a defined reader: a planner sets the reader, their goal, and the selection and ordering criteria, then a researcher curates and annotates each pick with why it matters, what it covers, and a suggested reading order.
- [Customer Case Study](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/case-study.md): Write a persuasive, evidence-backed customer success story in the classic challenge-solution-results arc: it first scopes the customer, the quantified before/after metrics, the approved customer quotes, and the single takeaway for prospects, then writes the case study with a results-forward summary, a relatable challenge, the solution narrative, and a measurable results section, then a review pass verifies every number and quote and the persuasive flow.
- [Customer Case Study](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/case-study-writeup.md): Write a persuasive customer/case-study writeup that turns a customer's results into a credible marketing asset — challenge, solution, and quantified results in the classic before/after arc, with a pull-quote and a clear CTA.
- [Daily Calendar & Prep Brief](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/calendar-brief.md): Assemble a morning brief from the day's calendar: a chronological agenda with per-meeting prep notes, conflicts flagged, and a short focus-time/priorities summary.
- [Daily Email Digest from a Corpus](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/corpus-email-digest.md): Produce an email-ready digest that summarizes a corpus of content (docs, feeds, notes) for a recurring send.
- [Dashboard Specification](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/dashboard-spec.md): Specify a dashboard from the questions it must answer, before anyone builds it — the artifact that prevents a chart-salad dashboard nobody uses.
- [Data Dictionary](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/data-dictionary.md): Document a dataset's schema as a clear, complete data dictionary so others can use it without guessing.
- [Data Quality Audit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/data-quality-audit.md): Audit a dataset against explicit data-quality rules and produce a scorecard of where it passes and fails across completeness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, and timeliness.
- [Data Visualization Explorer](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/data-viz-page.md): Build a single interactive chart or data explorer page — bar, line, scatter, or pie — driven by sample or provided data, with controls to filter, switch series, or change the dimension and a tooltip on hover.
- [Dataset to Narrative Report](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/data-to-report.md): Turn a dataset into a written, evidence-backed analytical report that a non-technical reader can act on.
- [Decision Evidence Brief](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/evidence-brief.md): Answer a specific decision question with a weighted, confidence-rated evidence brief: a planner frames the decision and the options, locks the evidence criteria and a confidence scale, a researcher gathers evidence for and against each option and rates the strength of each piece, and a copywriter writes a decision-oriented brief that states a recommendation with explicit confidence levels and the key uncertainties.
- [Deep Security Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/deep-security-review.md): Run a slow, thorough, WHOLE-CODEBASE security audit that looks for SYSTEMIC weaknesses — a vulnerability class repeated across many routes, a missing control at an architectural layer, inconsistent authorization, ad-hoc secret handling, a trust-boundary violation — not just isolated issues in one file.
- [Dependency Audit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/dependency-audit.md): Audit a project's dependencies for security, staleness, license, and maintenance risk, then produce a prioritized remediation report.
- [Deploy Checklist](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/deploy-checklist.md): Author and then actually execute a pre-deploy verification checklist for shipping a release to production — the concrete gates that must be green before the deploy button is pressed: tests passing, build clean, migrations reviewed, config/secrets present, feature flags set, rollback path confirmed, and observability/alerts ready.
- [Design System Consultation](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/design-system-consultation.md): Interview for product context and taste, then propose a full design system — type, color, layout, motion — and capture it as a DESIGN.md with live preview pages.
- [Design the Invitations](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/invitation-design.md): Produce the invitation the day deserves and get the facts beyond doubt: the date, time, venue, and RSVP instructions checked letter-for-letter against the event record — because a beautiful card with the wrong date is the classic disaster.
- [Diagnose + Add Database Indexes](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/db-index-tuning.md): Diagnose slow database queries and add the right indexes — driven by the query plan, not by hunches — then prove the speedup without harming writes.
- [Diagram from Text](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/diagram-from-text.md): Render a clear technical diagram — flowchart, architecture, sequence, ER, or org chart — from a plain-language description, as code-defined (Mermaid/Graphviz/SVG) so it is editable and version-controllable rather than a flat picture.
- [Digital Board Game](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/board-game-web.md): Build a single-file web version of a turn-based board game such as tic-tac-toe, checkers, connect-four, reversi, or a simple chess variant, with two-player hotseat or a basic AI opponent.
- [Documentation Drift Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/documentation-drift-review.md): Review project documentation against the code, configuration, commands, API surface, and shipped behavior to find stale or misleading guidance.
- [Documentation Rewrite](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/doc-rewrite.md): Rewrite confusing existing documentation into clear, scannable, task-oriented prose without losing any technical fact: it first audits the current doc to catalog every problem — buried steps, undefined jargon, missing prerequisites, broken structure — and locks a clarity checklist, then rewrites the doc to fix exactly those issues while preserving every accurate instruction.
- [Documentation Site](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/docs-site.md): Build a single-page documentation site with a sidebar table of contents, anchored sections, code blocks, and in-page navigation — the kind of reference page a library or API ships.
- [Domain Glossary](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/glossary-build.md): Build a consistent, accurate glossary for a domain: a planner sets the domain scope, the term-selection criteria, and the entry template, a researcher gathers the canonical definition and usage for each term with sources, and a copywriter writes the alphabetized glossary with cross-references and consistent entries.
- [Draft a Social Post](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/draft-social-post.md): Draft one social post from idea to approved copy.

- [Personal / Team Weekly Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/weekly-review.md): Assemble a reflective weekly review that pulls the week's done-list, metrics, and open loops into a structured retrospective with wins, misses, lessons, and next-week priorities.
- [Pest & Problem Diagnosis](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/pest-diagnosis.md): Turn 'something is wrong with the tomatoes' into a ranked differential: the likely culprits with the evidence for each, the gentlest treatment first, what to watch to confirm the diagnosis, and when to call in a professional — a garden clinic visit without the guesswork.
- [Photo Cull & Rank](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/photo-cull.md): Rank and cull a set of photos by objective quality — sharpness/focus, exposure, composition, eyes-open/expression for people, and duplicate-of-a-better-shot — to surface the keepers and justify the rejects.
- [Plan](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/plan.md): Author a PLAN for a piece of work as a reviewable draft task: a strong 'about', a set of outcomes (what should be created or updated at success), an ordered series of build steps each gated on a concrete static deliverable, and a final verification step that checks the outcomes were kept.
- [Plan the Episode](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/episode-plan.md): Turn the idea backlog and last episode's loose threads into a locked plan for the next episode: a rundown with timed segments, what to prep, and a record date — so the show ships on rhythm instead of on adrenaline.
- [Plan the Week](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/week-plan.md): Start Monday with the week already shaped: every meeting seen, the ones needing prep flagged, the conflicts and overload called out, and real focus blocks defended — a plan you made once, on purpose, instead of a calendar you react to all week.
- [Plan the Week's Dinners](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/weekly-menu-plan.md): Turn the pantry's real state into a planned week of dinners and one grocery list: check what is stocked, low, and out, plan seven dinners that use what is on hand and fit the household's tastes and schedule, write the menu onto the week, and produce a grocery list that covers the gaps.
- [Playtest Report](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/playtest-report.md): Playtest like it matters: a structured pass over the mechanics, the edge inputs, and the score loop, every finding written with its repro steps — a ranked fix list, not vibes.
- [Podcast Chapters & Show Notes](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/podcast-chaptering.md): Turn a podcast episode into navigable chapter markers plus publish-ready show notes — timestamped chapter titles, an episode summary, key takeaways, and linked mentions.
- [Portfolio Site](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/portfolio-site.md): Build a personal or professional portfolio site that showcases projects, an about/bio, and contact links in a single polished page.
- [Post-Event Thank-You Sweep](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/thank-you-sweep.md): Close the event the way it deserves: every gift-giver and every helper matched to a personal note, drafted in one sitting and tracked to sent — so 'the thank-yous actually go out' becomes a checklist instead of a lingering guilt.
- [PowerPoint from Content](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/powerpoint-deck.md): Turn source content into a real editable PowerPoint file (.pptx), not an HTML deck.
- [Practice Exam](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/practice-exam.md): Take the exam before the exam: a timed, self-scoring practice paper blueprinted from the deck — weighted toward what the review record says is weak — with an answer key that explains, not just grades.
- [Pre-Departure Countdown](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/pre-departure-countdown.md): Audit a trip's readiness in the final stretch before departure: verify documents and bookings, close the packing gaps against the packing roster, sweep home-prep tasks, and produce a day-by-day countdown checklist to the departure date — so the last week runs on a list, not on 3am worry.
- [Press Release](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/press-release.md): Write a professional, AP-style press release ready to send to journalists: it first locks the news angle, the five W's, the approved quote(s), and the boilerplate, then drafts the release in the standard format — dateline, inverted-pyramid lede, supporting body, quotes, boilerplate, and media contact — then a review pass enforces newsworthiness, factual accuracy, and house style.
- [Pricing Page](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/pricing-page.md): Build a single pricing or plan-comparison page with tiered plan cards, a feature comparison, a highlighted recommended plan, and optionally a monthly/annual toggle that updates prices.
- [Product Onboarding Tour](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/onboarding-flow.md): Build a single-file product onboarding tour or coachmark walkthrough that guides a new user through key features with sequential tooltips, a highlighted target, next/back/skip controls, and a finish state.
- [Project Config Scaffold](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/config-scaffold.md): Bootstrap a project's configuration — the tooling, linter, formatter, tsconfig/compiler, scripts, and ignore files — into a coherent, conflict-free baseline that actually works together.
- [Proposal / Statement of Work](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/proposal-sow.md): Draft a client proposal or statement of work that wins the deal and prevents scope creep — covering objectives, scope, deliverables, timeline/milestones, pricing, assumptions, and acceptance criteria.
- [Pull Request Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/pull-request-review.md): Staff-engineer-style PR review over a complete local PR corpus.
- [Quarterly Shoebox Summary](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/quarterly-summary.md): Close the quarter the way your accountant wishes everyone did: totals by category computed from the ledger entries themselves, the missing-documentation list naming each entry that lacks its paperwork, and the estimated-payment reminder in plain words.
- [Receipt Intake](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/receipt-intake.md): Empty the shoebox inbox properly: every waiting receipt becomes a dated, categorized ledger entry that names its source file, likely duplicates get flagged instead of double-counted, and the genuinely ambiguous ones become owner questions instead of guesses.
- [Receipts to Expense Ledger](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/receipt-ocr-ledger.md): Turn a folder of receipt photos/PDFs into a clean expense ledger: OCR each receipt, extract vendor, date, line items, tax, and total, assign an expense category, and reconcile that each extracted total matches its line items.
- [Reception Report](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/reception-report.md): The weekly reception review for your social posting.
- [Record a Relative](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/record-a-relative.md): Bank an elder's interview while the telling is fresh: file the transcript, pull the people, places, and dates into the family record with their source, and write the follow-up questions — because the questions you didn't ask are the ones that vanish.
- [Recurring Status Report](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/status-report.md): Produce a recurring (weekly/biweekly) status report by gathering signals from the team's tools and writing a tight, skimmable update for stakeholders.
- [Release Announcement](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/release-announcement.md): Write a public-facing release announcement that turns a shipped version into a compelling story for users — a blog-post / email-style piece that leads with the headline value, shows the marquee features with concrete before/after benefits, links to the full release notes and upgrade path, and ends with a clear call to action.
- [Release Artifact Sanity Check](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/release-artifact-sanity-check.md): Sanity-check a folder of release artifacts without executing them: inventory every package, verify hashes and signatures against trusted evidence, safely inspect every file inside archives and application bundles, scan for suspicious or secret-bearing content, and produce an evidence-backed ship or no-ship report.
- [Release Notes](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/release-notes.md): Turn a raw set of merged commits, pull requests, and ticket IDs into polished, human-readable release notes for a versioned release — grouped by theme (Features, Improvements, Bug Fixes, Breaking Changes), written for users rather than engineers, with upgrade/migration callouts surfaced first.
- [Release Readiness Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/release-readiness-review.md): Run a go/no-go release readiness review against a structured pre-launch checklist and produce a sign-off report with a clear ship decision.
- [Reliability & Resilience Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/reliability-review.md): Review a codebase for production reliability and resilience risks across asynchronous work, external dependencies, state transitions, resource lifecycles, and recovery paths.
- [Reorder Run](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/reorder-run.md): Turn a stock check into purchase orders: every item out or at its reorder point with the quantity that fills it back to par, grouped by supplier with lead times and costs, ready for a person to check and send.
- [Reproduce-Then-Fix a Bug](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/bug-fix-tdd.md): Fix a bug the disciplined way, with proof at every step: a failing test that reproduces it (verified red by a real test run), the smallest change at the real defect site, a green suite afterwards, and an enforced independent review of the fix.
- [Responsive HTML Email](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/email-template.md): Build a responsive HTML email template that renders across email clients — Outlook, Gmail, Apple Mail — using table-based layout, inline styles, and bulletproof buttons, for a newsletter, transactional, or promo send.
- [REST API Service](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/rest-api.md): Build a RESTful HTTP API service with resource endpoints, JSON request/response bodies, status codes, validation, and error handling.
- [Résumé / CV](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/resume-cv.md): Build a clean, ATS-friendly résumé or CV from a person's background, tailored to a target role.
- [Reusable Library Package](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/library-package.md): Build a reusable library/SDK with a clean public API surface, sensible defaults, and published documentation.
- [Reusable Web Component](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/web-component.md): Build a reusable custom element as a standards-based Web Component — a rating widget, toggle, accordion, modal, or color-picker — using the Custom Elements API and Shadow DOM with encapsulated styles, attributes, properties, and custom events.
- [Review a code folder](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/review-code-folder.md): A careful colleague's review of a folder of code: a short summary, each real problem with its file and line, how serious it is, what goes wrong and a suggested fix, and what the code does well.
- [Review Reply Batch](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/review-reply-batch.md): Draft replies to every customer review that still needs one, in the business's own voice: each reply thanks the reviewer, answers the specific point they raised, and mentions a fix only when the action list shows it under way.
- [Reviewer Loop](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/reviewer-loop.md): Draft → critique → revise (looped until approved) → publish.
- [Rollback Plan](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/rollback-plan.md): Author a concrete, tested rollback plan for a release so that when a deploy goes wrong the team can revert FAST and safely without improvising under pressure — covering the trigger conditions that mean 'roll back', the exact reversal steps (redeploy previous artifact, down-migrations, flag flips, cache/CDN invalidation), data-safety and forward/backward-compatibility considerations, the recovery-time estimate, and a post-rollback verification.
- [Root-Cause Investigation](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/root-cause-investigation.md): Debug systematically: reproduce the failure and find the true root cause before changing any code, then fix and verify.
- [Rough Cut Assembly](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/rough-cut-assembly.md): Execute the cut list and prove it ran: every clip verified against the media index before anything renders, the assembly driven through the project's media pipeline with a run log, and the result checked against the expected duration — an assembly you can trust unwatched.
- [RSS / Feed Digest](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/digest-from-feeds.md): Build a recurring digest from RSS/Atom feeds or news sources: fetch the latest items in the window, dedupe and cluster by topic, then write a scannable digest with one-line takes and source links.
- [Run of Show](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/run-of-show.md): Write the day-of run of show for a business event from the event desk: a timeline from vendor load-in to close with who is on point for each item, every vendor's arrival and contact, the catering count by dietary need, the contingencies, and the open items still to confirm.
- [Scaffold a Mod](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/mod-scaffold.md): Start the mod right: a correctly-shaped Minecraft datapack — pack.mcmeta carrying the right format number for the target game version, namespaced folders laid out properly, and one working example of the mod's core idea — plus install steps a twelve-year-old can follow.
- [Scheduled Backup or Export](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/backup-routine.md): Build a scheduled, idempotent backup/export routine that snapshots data (files, a database, or an app export) to a timestamped, optionally compressed destination, prunes old backups by a retention policy, and verifies each backup is restorable.
- [Scheduled Batch Job](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/cron-job.md): Build a scheduled batch job that runs on a cadence, processes a unit of work, is safe to re-run, and reports its outcome.
- [Schema / Type Migration](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/schema-migration.md): Migrate a schema or data shape with the expand/contract discipline: reads accept both shapes while the data moves, the old shape is dropped only after every record is transformed, and real suite runs between stages prove no record was ever stranded.
- [Scrape a Site to Structured Data](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/scrape-to-structured.md): Turn one or more web pages into a clean, structured dataset (JSON or CSV) with a fixed schema — product listings, directory entries, articles, tables, or job posts.
- [Seasonal Maintenance Sweep](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/seasonal-maintenance-sweep.md): Run a season's home-care sweep against the project's systems roster: work out what care is due or overdue from each system's interval, plan the walkthrough in a sensible order with supplies, then log the completed care and flag what needs a professional — leaving the roster's due-tracking reset and a short sweep report.
- [Security Architecture Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/security-architecture-review.md): A structured security architecture review: walk the stack for secrets, dependencies, auth, and common vulnerability classes, then report findings ranked by severity and confidence.
- [Security Review of a Diff](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/pr-security-review.md): Perform a focused security review of a code change or diff and produce a vulnerability report mapped to a threat checklist.
- [SEO Blog Post](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/blog-post.md): Write a complete, SEO-aware blog post that ranks and reads well: it locks the primary keyword, search intent, target reader, and a heading-by-heading outline FIRST, then drafts the full article in a single human voice with the keyword woven naturally into the title, intro, and H2s, and finally runs an editorial pass for clarity, flow, factual accuracy, and on-page SEO.
- [SEO Metadata Pack](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/seo-meta-pack.md): Generate a complete on-page SEO metadata pack for a set of pages: it first scopes each page's primary keyword and search intent and the length/format rules (title tag, meta description, Open Graph, Twitter card, slug), then writes optimized, unique metadata for every page that respects pixel/character limits and front-loads the keyword, producing a structured JSON file ready to drop into a CMS or templating layer.
- [Ship](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/ship.md): End-to-end release procedure: run tests, run a review pass, commit/push, open the PR, wait for CI to come back green, hand off for merge.
- [Simple Forecast / Trend Model](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/forecast-model.md): Build a simple, defensible forecast of a time series (revenue, demand, signups, usage) with the assumptions and method stated up front and the projection plus a confidence band as the output.
- [Slide Deck from Content](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/content-deck.md): Turn a body of source content into a presentation deck.
- [Social Digest](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/social-digest.md): The overnight read of your social feeds.
- [Social Media Thread](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/social-thread.md): Write a multi-post social thread (X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Threads) that hooks, delivers, and converts: it first locks the single angle/big idea, the platform and its character limits, the target reader, and the CTA, then drafts the thread as numbered posts with a scroll-stopping hook, one idea per post, and a clear close.
- [Source Quality Audit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/source-quality-audit.md): Once a month, make the reading list earn its place: score each source on what it actually delivered — accuracy, originality, noise — and keep, demote, or drop with evidence, so the brief stays sharp as the feeds drift.
- [Spec Authoring](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/spec-authoring.md): Turn a rough intent into a backlog-ready spec: interrogate scope and requirements against the real code, then file a well-formed, unambiguous issue.
- [Spreadsheet / Financial Model](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/spreadsheet-model.md): Build a working spreadsheet-style model (budget, forecast, unit economics, pricing, or scenario calculator) with clearly separated inputs, calculations, and outputs.
- [Standup / Team Update Summary](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/standup-summary.md): Condense a pile of raw team updates (standup messages, async check-ins, channel dumps) into one clean summary grouped by person or workstream, surfacing blockers and decisions.
- [Structured Interview Kit](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/structured-interview-kit.md): Write a structured interview kit for one role from the hiring desk: a job description built on the role's job-related requirements, two questions per requirement with follow-ups, a 1-to-4 scorecard with what each score looks like, and the questions to leave out.
- [Subtitle & Caption Generator](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/subtitle-generator.md): Generate time-synced subtitles/captions for a video in a standard caption format (SRT or WebVTT), so the video is accessible and watchable without sound.
- [Summarize a Long Document](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/summarize-long.md): Distill a long document into a faithful, well-structured summary at a chosen depth: it first scopes the audience, the target length and format (TL;DR line, executive summary, or bulleted key points), and what the reader must take away, then writes the summary capturing every major point and decision in proportion, with nothing invented and nothing critical dropped.
- [Survey Analysis](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/survey-analysis.md): Analyze survey responses into a clear summary of what respondents actually said, across both quantitative (rating/multiple-choice) and open-text questions.
- [Tailor Résumé to a Posting](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/tailor-resume.md): Adapt an EXISTING résumé to a specific job posting — a fit map of must-hit requirements first, then a tailored variant that re-orders and re-words real experience without inventing any.
- [Tailored Cover Letter](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/cover-letter.md): Write a tailored, one-page cover letter that maps a candidate's real background to a specific job's requirements: it first scopes the role's key requirements, the company hook, and the 3-4 strongest matching proof points from the applicant's experience, then drafts a focused letter with a specific opening, evidence-backed body paragraphs, and a confident close.
- [Targeted Performance Fix](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/perf-optimization.md): Make a measured, targeted performance improvement: baseline numbers recorded with their method before anything changes, one bottleneck fixed in reversible stages with the suite green, the same measurement re-run to prove the gain, and an enforced independent review.
- [Team Handbook Section](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/handbook-section.md): Write a clear, reference-grade section of a team/company handbook — a policy, process, or how-we-work doc that a new hire can read once and act on correctly.
- [Technical Design Doc](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/spec-doc.md): Write a technical design document (RFC / engineering design doc) that gets a system change reviewed and approved — covering context and problem, goals and non-goals, the proposed design, alternatives considered, trade-offs, risks, and a rollout plan.
- [Technical Documentation](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/technical-documentation.md): Generate a coherent documentation set from a codebase, organized by the Diataxis model (tutorials, how-to guides, reference, explanation), with cross-links and a coverage pass.
- [Test Coverage Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/test-coverage-review.md): Review a codebase or module's test suite for real coverage and quality, then produce a gap report and a prioritized backlog of tests to add.
- [Test Suite Backfill](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/test-suite-backfill.md): Add tests that actually bite to untested code: rank the untested behavior by breakage cost, write tests in the project's real layout that a wrong implementation would fail, and prove the suite green with real run receipts — under an enforced independent review.
- [Text-to-Speech a Folder](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/folder-to-audio.md): Turn a folder of text files (articles, chapters, notes, markdown) into a set of spoken audio files using text-to-speech, so a reading list becomes a listening list.
- [Thank-You Note Batch](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/thank-you-batch.md): Clear the owed-thanks list with notes that sound like you: read who is owed and for what from the correspondence roster, draft one note per person that names the actual gift or kindness — no template smell — then log every note so nobody who mattered goes unanswered.
- [Thumbnail Generator](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/thumbnail-generator.md): Derive a consistent set of thumbnails or responsive size-variants from a folder of source images — square crops for grids, srcset widths for the web, smart-cropped to keep the subject centered — and emit them with predictable names.
- [Tidy up a spreadsheet](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/tidy-spreadsheet.md): Clean up a messy CSV or TSV file: trims stray spaces, puts email addresses in lower case and dates in one format, settles on one spelling of each repeated value, and removes duplicate rows.
- [Tileset Batch](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/tileset-batch.md): Produce a style-locked batch of tiles and account for every one: named to the convention, sized to spec, generated against the library's style anchor, and appended to the manifest with tags — an asset library a game engine can trust, not a folder of maybes.
- [Topic Explainer](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/topic-explainer.md): Explain a complex topic clearly for a defined audience: a planner pins the audience, their assumed prior knowledge, and the concepts that must be taught, a researcher gathers accurate facts and good analogies with sources, and a copywriter writes a progressively-structured explainer that builds from fundamentals to the full picture.
- [Track Prices Over Time](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/price-tracker.md): Build a price tracker that records the price of one or more products/SKUs each time it runs, appending a timestamped history so you can see trends, drops, and the lowest price seen.
- [Transcribe and Index a Tape](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/transcribe-index.md): Give one tape the ten-second-findability treatment: transcript on file, then every moment worth finding indexed with its timecode and people tags — so 'the clip of Opa's 80th toast' becomes a query, not an afternoon of scrubbing.
- [Transcribe Audio or Video](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/transcribe-audio.md): Convert an audio or video recording into an accurate, readable transcript using speech-to-text, with speaker labels and timestamps.
- [Transcript to Shownotes](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/transcribe-and-shownotes.md): Take a finished recording from raw transcript to publishable shownotes: a clean transcript on file, timestamped chapters, a summary listeners actually read, and the links mentioned — the per-episode ritual that turns audio into an archive.
- [Translate Content](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/translate-content.md): Translate the project's new and changed content into the designated language as sidecar files under translations/<language>/, mirroring the source structure and never modifying originals.
- [Type-Safety Pass](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/type-safety-pass.md): Tighten a module against unsafe patterns — loose equality, implicit coercions, swallowed catches, untyped boundaries, any-casts — with counted evidence: an audit that inventories the patterns by a stated method, fixes that never silence a check to move a count, a same-method re-count, and an enforced independent review.
- [Typed SDK Wrapper for an External API](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/sdk-wrapper.md): Wrap a third-party HTTP API as a clean, typed client library — studying the real API surface first so the wrapper matches reality, not guesses.
- [Upgrade a Dependency](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/dependency-upgrade.md): Upgrade dependencies in reviewable stages with proof at every step: a green suite before any bump, smallest-risk-first ordering, call-site adaptations at their real locations, a real suite run between stages, and an honest revert for anything that cannot go green.
- [UX & Visual Design Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/design-review.md): Critique a UI's user experience and visual design and produce a prioritized design-review report.
- [Version Bump](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/version-bump.md): Perform a coordinated, semver-correct version bump across a project — deciding MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH from the actual change set, then updating every place the version is stamped in lockstep (package manifest(s), version constant, lockfile, badges, docs) plus the changelog header, so nothing drifts out of sync.
- [Video Storyboard from a Script](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/video-storyboard.md): Turn a video script into a shot-by-shot storyboard — each scene broken into shots with a framing sketch/description, camera direction, on-screen action, the matching script line, and timing — so a shoot or animation has a clear visual plan.
- [Visual Moodboard](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/moodboard.md): Compose a visual moodboard that captures a direction — palette, textures, type vibe, imagery, and reference tiles — from a written brief, so a team can align on a look before any production work begins.
- [Voiceover / TTS Script](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/voiceover-script.md): Write a voiceover script tuned for spoken delivery — by a human VO artist or a text-to-speech engine — for a video, ad, explainer, or narration, with pacing, pronunciation, and timing baked in.
- [Watch a Page or API and Alert](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/monitor-and-alert.md): Build a watcher that polls a web page or API endpoint on a schedule, detects a meaningful change or threshold breach, and fires an alert (and only alerts on real changes, not noise).
- [Weak-Spot Drill](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/weak-spot-drill.md): Stop practicing what you already know: read the review record, name the actual weak spots with the numbers as evidence, and build a short targeted drill plus the follow-up schedule that closes them.
- [Weave a Chapter](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/chapter-weave.md): Weave the banked sessions into one memoir chapter in the teller's voice: every scene traceable to something actually said, gaps marked for a future session instead of invented — the ritual that turns interviews into a book.
- [Weekly Garden Walkthrough](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/weekly-walkthrough.md): Walk the beds once a week with a plan instead of a vague worry: what each bed needs this week derived from the plantings and the season, the walkthrough ordered so it actually gets done, and the observations and harvests logged so the almanac accrues.
- [Weekly Pipeline Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/weekly-pipeline-review.md): The weekly walk of a job-search pipeline — a grounded snapshot of every application (what moved in the last seven days, what went stale, which follow-ups are due), then a review that chases or consciously parks every stalled item and commits to exactly three concrete priorities for next week.
- [Weekly Schedule Draft](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/weekly-schedule-draft.md): Draft a week's shift schedule from the roster: every open spot filled from who is available, hours kept inside the limits the business set, the spots nobody can take named plainly, and the whole week left for a person to approve.
- [Whitepaper](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/whitepaper.md): Author a long-form, authoritative whitepaper that makes a researched argument — a technical position paper, industry analysis, or thought-leadership piece with citations.
- [Word Document from Content or Research](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/research-to-document.md): Turn supplied content or a researched question into a real Word document (.docx, plus PDF on request) with DocBlocks.
- [Write an Automation Recipe](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/automation-recipe.md): Turn 'I wish the house would...' into an inspectable, versioned automation: triggers and actions that name real devices from the house's own inventory, a dry run through the device tools before anything is armed, and a manual override always written in.
- [Year in Review](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/year-in-review.md): Build the year-in-review that makes someone cry the good way: every month represented or its gap acknowledged, the people balanced, the closing image chosen on purpose — the annual ritual the whole photo archive exists for.
- [YouTube Chapters & SEO Metadata](https://gezel.com/docs/craftbook/youtube-chapters-seo.md): Turn a video (or its transcript) into a complete, paste-ready YouTube publishing kit — SEO title options, an optimized description with timestamped chapters, tags/keywords, and thumbnail text ideas — so an upload ranks and is navigable.

## Project Types

- [Every project type](https://gezel.com/docs/project-types-index.md): Ready-made project setups: crew, plans, and toolsets in one.
- [Books & Month Close](https://gezel.com/docs/project-type/books-and-close.md): Keep the books tidy and close each month on time.
- [Campaign Room](https://gezel.com/docs/project-type/campaign-room.md): Run one marketing campaign from plan to results.
- [Caregiving Binder](https://gezel.com/docs/project-type/caregiving-binder.md): Coordinate a loved one's care without losing the thread.

- [Image Feed](https://gezel.com/docs/project-type/image-feed.md): A visual feed with a working rhythm — your social media writer runs the posting pipeline, an image maker turns notions into pictures in the feed's own style, and a live gallery shows every post from first idea to published.

## Technical

- [How gezel runs: app, daemon, and tools](https://gezel.com/docs/architecture.md): The desktop app, the background service, and how Gezel acts.
- [Where files live](https://gezel.com/docs/where-files-live.md): The gezel home folder, mapped.
- [Providers and engines](https://gezel.com/docs/providers-and-engines.md): Working with cloud models through the Claude and Codex CLIs or the Claude and OpenAI APIs, local engines, and how credentials are handled.
- [Tools and toolsets](https://gezel.com/docs/tools-and-toolsets.md): Every built-in tool group and what it lets Gezel do.
- [Add-on toolsets and connectors](https://gezel.com/docs/toolset-catalog.md): Toolsets you can add to a crew member, and connectors that bring outside data into a project.
- [The security model: tokens, sandboxing, and consent](https://gezel.com/docs/security-model.md): The guardrails between Gezel and your computer.
- [What leaves this computer](https://gezel.com/docs/what-leaves-this-computer.md): Every kind of network traffic Gezel can make, and which security level allows it.
- [Verifying your download](https://gezel.com/docs/verifying-your-download.md): Checking that the installer you downloaded is the one we published.
- [Governance: who writes Gezel, and how](https://gezel.com/docs/governance.md): Open source, not open contribution — how proposals reach a release, how changes are checked, and what keeps working if we stop.
- [How knowledge works in Gezel](https://gezel.com/docs/how-knowledge-works.md): The storage, embeddings, hybrid search, and portable .gezk catalogs behind Gezel's knowledge.
- [The gezel command line](https://gezel.com/docs/cli-reference.md): Headless Gezel — start the service, run one-shot work, export docs.
- [Gezel on npm: the package map](https://gezel.com/docs/npm-packages.md): Choose the command line, SDK, daemon, client, or lower-level package for your integration.
- [Working with knowledge catalogs](https://gezel.com/docs/knowledge-command-line.md): Build, validate, search, install, remove, and export .gezk catalogs with the gezel command line.
- [Writing scripts with gezel-sdk](https://gezel.com/docs/writing-scripts-with-gezel-sdk.md): Build typed, capability-limited automations that run inside a Gezel project.
- [Building connected apps with gezel-app-sdk](https://gezel.com/docs/building-connected-apps-with-gezel-app-sdk.md): Discover Gezel, ask for user consent, and use local models or product APIs from another app.
- [Gezel on a server](https://gezel.com/docs/gezel-on-a-server.md): Run the Gezel service headless, under your own account, with the security level and activity mode a server should have.
- [Build a Gezel app: the complete guide](https://gezel.com/docs/build-a-gezel-app.md): Everything a person or an AI agent needs to build a Gezel app on one page, from the working loop and the rules to the four maintained guides.
- [Building AI Apps inside Gezel](https://gezel.com/docs/building-ai-apps-inside-gezel.md): Combine a project type, dashboard, crew, craftbooks, scripts, and data into one reusable Gezel experience.
- [Gezel in Docker](https://gezel.com/docs/gezel-in-docker.md): One command runs Gezel in a container, with every engine inside. Use Gezel from your browser, give your other apps local AI, or put Gezel to work on a folder.
- [How DocBlocks uses Gezel for text AI](https://gezel.com/docs/docblocks-text-ai-with-gezel.md): A developer walkthrough of consent, private hosting, streamed writing, knowledge retrieval, and the shared embedding APIs that simplify an editor integration.
- [How we test models](https://gezel.com/docs/how-we-test-models.md): What the model scores mean, how they are measured, and what they don't tell you.
- [Using the Gezel page APIs](https://gezel.com/docs/gezel-page-apis.md): Connect an app page to project files, file viewers, DuckDB summaries, declared actions, and the host theme.
- [Gezel app page style guide](https://gezel.com/docs/gezel-app-page-style-guide.md): What Gezel supplies to app pages, and how to build consistent typography, themes, layouts, and controls.
- [Model scorecard](https://gezel.com/docs/model-scorecard.md): Measured results for every model we have tested, on each task set.
- [Gezel app UX guide](https://gezel.com/docs/gezel-app-ux-guide.md): How a Gezel app is organized and how people act in it — Home, a tab per noun, Settings, action keys that open dialogs, and actions on the records themselves.
- [Every model](https://gezel.com/docs/model-catalog.md): Every AI model Gezel can run on your own computer, with size, context and license.

## What's New

- [What's new](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new-index.md): Every gezel release, in plain language — what changed and what it means for you.
- [1.26315 — 11 November 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26315.md): Add your own models from Hugging Face or a file, apps that update themselves, Back and Forward in the title bar, and Help and Plans as new names.
- [1.26313 — 9 November 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26313.md): Connectors for every project, local models on AMD Radeon graphics, a large Qwen model on Macs with less memory, and links on gezel.com that open the app.
- [1.26307 — 3 November 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26307.md): Change a picture you already have, give pictures a style, test a model on your own computer, start one of nineteen new projects for a small business, and run gezel in Docker.
- [1.26300 — 27 October 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26300.md): Cameras that keep an eye on a room, new views of what is in your folders, Gezel's tools inside Claude Code and Codex, and pairing another computer with a code.
- [1.26287 — 14 October 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26287.md): Hand your crew a folder to look after overnight, a much simpler first start, a chat about the open document inside Office, and photos found by what is in them.
- [1.26279 — 6 October 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26279.md): One Activity panel for everything going on, gezels that cite their sources, Mac chats that go ahead of background work, and catalog searches that find the right page.
- [1.26275 — 2 October 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26275.md): Quicker follow-ups from local models, reviews that really send work back, diagrams in Word, and read-only projects that stay read-only.
- [1.26274 — 1 October 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26274.md): Craftbook tasks that stall far less, finished work handed back as a file you can open, whole replies read aloud, and fewer off-topic passages in chat.
- [1.26273 — 30 September 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26273.md): Start a craftbook from your message, get finished work back with its sums checked, search seventeen Wikipedia shelves offline, and let one gezel carry a whole task.
- [1.26261 — 18 September 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26261.md): Visible routes for requested files, sharper knowledge search, stronger command-line batch workflows, and app-hosted Gezel for developers.
- [1.26251 — 8 September 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26251.md): Engines that reserve memory instead of colliding, llama.cpp v0.4 loading controls, GLM 5.3 on DwarfStar, and catalogs built from a folder of Markdown.
- [1.26247 — 4 September 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26247.md): Spreadsheets you can sort, filter and edit in place, conversations that make their own room, drafts that survive a restart, and a Village with real streets.
- [1.26244 — 1 September 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26244.md): Spreadsheets your crew can actually count, documents read aloud, dictation and spell-checking, and local models that stop stalling out at five minutes.
- [1.26237 — 25 August 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26237.md): Change proposals you read before any file is edited, fixes drafted overnight, a Try again button for stuck tasks, and AI Apps you can share as a link.
- [1.26234 — 22 August 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26234.md): Reference libraries your crew can cite, gezels that look things up on their own, links between projects, and people grouped in your photos.
- [1.26231 — 19 August 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26231.md): A live dashboard on your desktop wallpaper, disk space you can see and reclaim, backup and restore, your local models inside VS Code, and Qwen 3.8 27B tops the scorecard.
- [1.26226 — 14 August 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26226.md): Five more models on the scorecard, file problems you can hand straight to a gezel, a much fuller terminal app, and memory that keeps working when its index breaks.
- [1.26224 — 12 August 2026](https://gezel.com/docs/whats-new/1.26224.md): Measured model scores, per-model memory controls, editable Office documents, and much stricter rules about what a gezel may install.
